parties.ourParty: The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company) — customer/licensee under this site development and hosting arrangement

plans.note: No liability heading is surfaced in the outline, but development/hosting agreements normally place a cap and disclaimer in the later general/operational articles. Sweep the unmapped body under sec-p0001 and the Article 5 area around sec-5.4 for any cap, consequential-damages waiver or exclusive-remedy language; confirm mutuality and carve-outs for IP infringement, confidentiality and willful misconduct before concluding the rule is unmet.

Vendor IP-infringement and misconduct indemnity would sit in the same back-end article group as liability. Check the unmapped text under sec-p0001 and around sec-5.4; note whether any indemnity is one-way against the Company (content/Deerskin Products materials), which would need narrowing rather than deletion. Flag as missing only if no indemnity appears anywhere.

Nothing in the outline suggests a covenant restricting the Company's businesses or product sourcing. Still scan the Article 1 scope text near sec-1.4 for any 'shall not develop or operate a competing site' language; absent that, record as not present rather than a deviation.

A hosting/development deal for the Deerskin Products site frequently makes HDI the sole developer or host. Sec-1.4 (access rights) and the surrounding Article 1 scope text are the most likely home for a sole-source or 'HDI shall be the exclusive host' obligation on the Company; check whether any exclusivity is time-boxed and exit-linked to the Termination Date.

No pricing or fee section is exposed in the outline. Direction rule: only an MFN obliging the Company to give HDI best terms is objectionable; an MFN in our favour is welcome. Scan any fees/charges text under sec-p0001, but expect none.

Sec-5.4 deals with each party appointing a representative/coordinator, which is the natural neighbourhood for a personnel non-solicit if one exists. Read the paragraphs immediately following sec-5.4; if a non-solicit binds the Company, test duration, scope and whether general advertising and unsolicited applicants are carved out.

The defined term 'Termination Date' confirms a termination article exists even though it is not surfaced as a heading. Locate it in the unmapped body under sec-p0001; check whether the Company may terminate on notice without penalty and whether HDI holds a symmetric or broader walk-away right mid-term.

Term and renewal mechanics sit with the termination provisions signalled by 'Termination Date'. Look in the unmapped Article 1/term text under sec-p0001 for auto-renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any price uplift; a fixed term with no auto-renewal satisfies the rule.

Governing law and venue are boilerplate in the final article, i.e. the Article 5 block containing sec-5.4 and immediately before the signature block at sec-p0072. Both parties are US entities, so New York or Delaware is expected and acceptable; only foreign law or mandatory offshore arbitration would be a deviation.

Assignment/successors language belongs in the same Article 5 boilerplate run as sec-5.4, just ahead of the sec-p0072 signature block. Confirm the Company may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger, and that HDI has no termination right triggered by our change of control (relevant given the corporate relationship between these parties).

Sec-1.4 grants the Company access to something HDI controls, so the ownership allocation for the developed site, Deerskin Products content and Company data should be nearby in Article 1 or the following article. Direction rule: confirm the Company owns its data, marks and paid-for deliverables and that nothing assigns Company IP to HDI; a licence-back to HDI limited to performing the services is acceptable.

Sec-1.4 is the access/licence hook ('HDI shall provide the Company with access to...'). Test scope: whether the grant extends to Company affiliates and contractors, and whether it is revocable at will or suspendable by HDI outside a payment default.

No audit or records heading appears in the outline. If HDI holds usage or records inspection rights, they would follow the fees or reporting text under sec-p0001; test notice, frequency, off-site preference and who bears cost. Otherwise record as not present.

Direction rule: service credits running to the Company are fine; only liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Company are objectionable. Check any fee, late-payment or early-termination text in the unmapped body under sec-p0001 for a stipulated-damages formula; none is visible in the outline.

Development and hosting work should carry an HDI performance/services warranty with a re-performance remedy, plus availability commitments. Search the unmapped articles under sec-p0001 (and the service description around sec-1.4) for warranty or 'AS IS' disclaimer language; a bare disclaimer with no affirmative warranty is a deviation.

No insurance heading is surfaced. HDI hosts the site and touches Company data, so the rule expects coverage; check the Article 5 boilerplate near sec-5.4 before concluding. If nothing appears, treat as missing and note that an affiliate-style arrangement may explain the omission.

No fees or volume schedule is exposed in the outline. Scan the unmapped payment terms under sec-p0001 for minimum spend, take-or-pay or guaranteed-volume language binding the Company; if a minimum exists, confirm an exit or reduction path tied to the Termination Date.

The 'Termination Date' definition implies an effects-of-termination provision where transition assistance and return of Company data/site content would live; the access mechanics in sec-1.4 may also carry a post-termination data retrieval right. Confirm the Company gets its data back in usable form and reasonable migration help, or mark missing.
